evals.name: triage-cascade-from-recorded-runs
evals.prompt: Triage costs us too much on Sonnet. We ran the triage eval on haiku, sonnet and opus last week, results are in evals/triage/results. Pick the cheapest setup that still meets the bar in the triage solution doc and set the route.
evals.expected_output: route_frontier.py run on the three recorded files at threshold 0.85 from docs/genai/triage-solution.md; the frontier prints six options (three static, three cascades) and chooses cascade claude-haiku-4-5->claude-sonnet-5-5 (lower 0.883, $1.58 per 1k, 20.0% escalated) over static Sonnet ($2.18 per 1k); llm/routing.yaml routes.triage becomes strategy cascade with legs first and then, each naming a models: key with its own effort (null on the claude-haiku-4-5 leg, never inherited from the balanced tier), max_tokens and timeout_s, escalate_on [invalid, refusal, max_tokens], a budget_usd_month and the frontier line as evidence; docs/genai/routing.md holds the row with a monthly estimate at 20,000 calls a day and a re-run date; prices come from the routing.yaml price table, not memory.
expectations: The transcript runs route_frontier.py on evals/triage/results/haiku.jsonl, sonnet.jsonl and opus.jsonl with --threshold 0.85, and copies its option lines and its route-frontier line verbatim
The threshold 0.85 is taken from docs/genai/triage-solution.md, not asked for or invented
It chooses cascade claude-haiku-4-5->claude-sonnet-5-5 from the frontier line (lower 0.883 at or above 0.85, $1.58 per 1k, escalated 20.0%) rather than static claude-sonnet-5-5 at $2.18 per 1k

llm/routing.yaml routes.triage gains strategy: cascade, cascade with first claude-haiku-4-5 and then claude-sonnet-5-5 (both keys of models:), escalate_on [invalid, refusal, max_tokens] and a budget_usd_month, with the frontier line and a date as a comment
Each cascade leg carries its own effort, max_tokens and timeout_s: the claude-haiku-4-5 leg has effort null (Haiku 4.5 rejects effort), so it does not inherit the route's balanced tier effort
A monthly estimate is given from the 20,000 calls a day in the README and the frontier's cost per 1k, with the current static Sonnet cost beside it
docs/genai/routing.md has a row for triage with the chosen route, the score, the cost per 1,000 and a re-run date (when a model id or price changes, or 90 days)
It does not quote a price from memory: every price or cost it states comes from llm/routing.yaml or from route_frontier.py output
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: fallback-contaminated-candidate
evals.prompt: compare haiku and sonnet for triage using the runs in evals/triage/results and switch the route to whichever is cheaper but still passes
evals.expected_output: route_frontier.py refuses the Sonnet file with exit 2 because it holds rows from claude-haiku-4-5 (the route's fallback answered six cases during the run); the skill does not choose a route from it, leaves llm/routing.yaml unchanged, says the Sonnet eval must be re-run with the override (which now runs with no fallback), and gives the command to re-run it.
expectations: The transcript runs route_frontier.py on the two files and reports that evals/triage/results/sonnet.jsonl holds models claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-haiku-4-5, that is a fallback ran during the eval
It refuses the Sonnet candidate and asks for a re-run of the Sonnet eval, naming the command (make eval EVAL=triage MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5 or the harness with --model)
llm/routing.yaml routes.triage is not changed to a new model or strategy on the strength of these files
It does not drop the haiku rows from the Sonnet file and score the rest as if it were a clean Sonnet run
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
